messages:
acme-net-admin: Hey team — since our cert rotation yesterday we've had intermittent failures during the mTLS handshake to Redwood Private control plane. App logs show `tls: handshake failure` and the control plane closes with `alert bad certificate`.
acme-net-admin: Repro steps: 1) From inside our VPC run `openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example.com:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca_bundle.pem -servername control.redwood.example.com` 2) repeat ~50x concurrently. ~20% of connections get `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate` or the connection immediately resets.
acme-net-admin: tcpdump snippet attached (paste):
```
14:02:11.123456 IP 10.0.2.15.443 > 10.0.3.22.53422: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 229, length 511
TLSv1.3 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Client Hello
14:02:11.123789 IP 10.0.3.22.53422 > 10.0.2.15.443: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0  # immediate reset
```
acme-net-admin: We also see intermittent `OCSP response missing` in the client-side logs. Our network team suspects an egress allowlist or proxy is dropping traffic to OCSP/CRL endpoints.
jamie_sre: Thanks for the detail. Can you confirm whether your environment proxies outbound HTTPS and whether any TLS-inspecting/terminating firewall sits in the path? Also, which client cert type are you using (RSA vs ECDSA) and which CA bundle?
acme-net-admin: We do have an egress proxy (apac-egress-proxy.company.local) that does transparent TLS inspection for some subnets. Certs are ECDSA P-256 signed by our internal intermediate CA, chained to a corporate root. We provide the full chain in `ca_bundle.pem`.
maria_support: @acme-net-admin can you run a quick openssl s_client with `-status` to force OCSP stapling check and paste the output? Example: `openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example.com:443 -status -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca_bundle.pem -servername control.redwood.example.com` — we want to see if the server is stapling OCSP and whether your proxy is stripping it.
acme-net-admin: Ran it, server stapling sometimes absent. Sample output:
```
OCSP response: no response sent
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```
kai_infra: Two quick angles: 1) If the egress proxy is re-signing server certs for inspection, it can break the TLS 1.3 post-handshake and OCSP stapling behavior. 2) Client cert chain validation can fail if intermediate CA is not present or if the proxy rewrites the chain. Can you capture the server cert chain from both a working and failing attempt and paste the subjects/issuers?
acme-net-admin: Working attempt chain:
- subject CN=control.redwood.example.com issuer CN=Redwood Control Plane Intermediate
- issuer CN=Redwood Control Plane Intermediate issuer CN=Redwood Root CA
Failing attempt: the server cert in the capture shows issuer CN=Corporate TLS Inspect CA (our proxy) which explains `unable to get local issuer certificate` (client doesn't trust that CA).
jamie_sre: That strongly suggests the egress TLS inspection is intercepting some connections and replacing the server cert; because mTLS requires the server present an unmodified chain for client verification (and OCSP stapling too), inspection will break mTLS unless the proxy forwards the original chain or is trusted by both sides. Two mitigate options:
- Whitelist control.redwood.example.com in your proxy so it does no interception for that FQDN (SNI-based passthrough).
- Add the proxy's inspection CA to the client trust store (risky) and ensure it forwards OCSP/CRL responses.
maria_support: Also, can you confirm whether your proxy allows outbound TCP to port 80/443 to external OCSP responders or only allows through the proxy? We saw `OCSP response missing` — if the proxy blocks direct OCSP retrieving or strips stapled responses, we get intermittent failures.
acme-net-admin: Proxy blocked direct egress to ocsp.* endpoints; only allowed via the proxy which terminates TLS. We can ask the network team to add an allowlist for ocsp.redwood.example.com and crl.redwood.example.com.
kai_infra: FYI, on our side control plane will accept connections as long as client cert verifies and OCSP checks pass. We do prefer stapled OCSP, but also perform OCSP queries from our control plane to the issuer. If your proxy alters the cert chain, our checks may return REVOKED/UNKNOWN and close the connection.
deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-21345 — label: customer-mtls-handshake — assigned to eng-security and SRE oncall.
eng-security: We'll need a PCAP from both sides for a failing handshake, plus the systemd journal for the client agent (or container logs) around the failure timestamp. Also please include `openssl s_client -connect ... -showcerts -status` output for the failing attempt.
acme-net-admin: Uploading PCAP to the ticket now, and granting temporary VPN access for a debug session. We've added ocsp.redwood.example.com and crl.redwood.example.com to the allowlist in a canary subnet — testing now.
acme-net-admin: Update: After allowlisting OCSP endpoints and whitelisting control.redwood.example.com for SNI passthrough, failures dropped to ~0.5% during a 10k-req test. Looks much better.
jamie_sre: Great. For permanent fix we recommend: 1) SNI passthrough for all Redwood control plane hostnames OR an explicit exemption for the control plane certificate chain. 2) Ensure proxy preserves TLS 1.3 features (no active MITM for these FQDNs). 3) If you must intercept, distribute the inspection CA to all client trust stores and coordinate OCSP forwarding behavior.
acme-net-admin: We'll implement passthrough in our global rule set and monitor. Thanks for the fast help. :raised_hands:
maria_support: Marking this thread as resolved after 24h stable. Please re-open if anything reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
jamie_sre: Noted — closing on our side once ticket INC-21345 is updated with root cause and remediation steps.
